articles.headline: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
articles.description: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
articles.headlineJa: 現役NFL選手たちが、いかにして歴代サック数ランキングを塗り替え続けているか
articles.descriptionJa: マイルズ・ギャレットが歴代サック数ランキングを猛烈なペースで駆け上がる中、現役選手たちが伝説的な名手たちの記録に迫っている。
articles.body:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns.

This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams after a blockbuster trade in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season.

Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players -- Von Miller (No. 9), Cameron Jordan (No. 17), Calais Campbell (No. 25), T.J. Watt (No. 26), Danielle Hunter (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack (T-29th) -- in the top 30. 

Joining the top 30 soon could be Aaron Donald, who unretired to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th. 

As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory.

Miller, who signed with the Dallas Cowboys in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.  

But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982.

If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's. 

As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape

We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season.

Week 6 update

With Garrett still out, it was another quiet week on the sack front. Of the active leaders, it was the oldest that recorded the lone sack of the week in Campbell. He moved back in front of Hunter. 

Week 5 update

Hunter was the only player among the active leaders to record a sack this week, moving him ahead of Campbell to No. 26 all-time. Hunter now has three sacks through five games. 

Week 4 update

Watt kicked off things in Week 4 on "Thursday Night Football" in an impactful way. He had one sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery to move his total to 4.5 sacks on the season. Other than that, there wasn't much activity with Garrett continuing to be on IR.

articles.headline: Jalen Hurts out for season after blood clots discovered in Eagles QB's lungs
articles.description: Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the Eagles QB's lungs, according to NFL Network and ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: イーグルスのQBジェイレン・ハーツ、肺に血栓が見つかり今季絶望
articles.descriptionJa: NFLネットワークおよびESPNによると、医師が肺に複数の血栓を発見したため、イーグルスのQBジェイレン・ハーツは今シーズンの残り全ての試合を欠場することになった。
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback's lungs, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Hurts will undergo treatment for the blood clots that will take at least three months, according to Rapoport.

Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts' medical status.

articles.headline: Sources: Falcons to sign QB Andy Dalton, release QB Cooper Rush
articles.description: The Falcons are signing quarterback Andy Dalton, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday, and are are releasing quarterback Cooper Rush, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported.
articles.headlineJa: 【情報】ファルコンズ、QBアンディ・ダルトンと契約し、QBクーパー・ラッシュを解雇へ
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜日、ESPNのアダム・シェフターに情報筋が伝えたところによると、ファルコンズはQBアンディ・ダルトンと契約する。また、NFLネットワークのイアン・ラポポートは、同チームがQBクーパー・ラッシュを解雇すると報じた。
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are signing veteran quarterback Andy Dalton, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are releasing quarterback Cooper Rush, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported.

Dalton was most recently with the Philadelphia Eagles. He was released Oct. 9. Dalton started seven games for the Carolina Panthers from 2023 to 2025 and has started 169 games overall in 16 seasons.

The Falcons have been carrying four quarterbacks on their roster since training camp: starter Michael Penix Jr., Tua Tagovailoa, Rush and undrafted rookie Jack Strand.

Rush started the first two games of the season with both Penix (ACL) and Tagovailoa (oblique) sidelined. The Falcons scored a combined 16 points in those games, a league low.

Penix came out of the team's Week 5 game against the Baltimore Ravens, an eventual loss, with a rib injury. Tagovailoa replaced Penix in overtime and threw the game-ending interception.

Penix was able to play Sunday in Atlanta's 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears. Penix was sacked five times by the Bears, but said he came away from the game healthy and his ribs were not an issue.

Dalton, a 16-year veteran, had one pass attempt this season and it went for an interception. In his career, Dalton has 84 wins as a starter with a 62.6% completion percentage for 39,793 passing yards with 254 touchdowns and 152 interceptions. He was the Cincinnati Bengals' primary quarterback from 2011 to 2019.

articles.headline: Who could replace Carrick after Man United's worst start since 1986?
articles.description: Manchester United have struggled this season, but which managers could step in to replace Michael Carrick if the club sack him?
articles.body:
Manchester United have made their worst start to a league season since 1986. They exited the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle last month and are closer to the Premier League relegation zone than the top four following Sunday's 1-1 draw at Leeds United, so the pressure is mounting on manager Michael Carrick.

That trip to Elland Road extended United's winless run in all competitions to six games ahead of Wednesday's UEFA Champions League trip to Serie A's Como. But Carrick said that the result against Daniel Farke's side marked a "fresh start" for his team.

United have dismissed a manager in each of the past two seasons, however -- Erik ten Hag was fired in October 2024, followed by Ruben Amorim in January 2026.

So with results continuing to disappoint and Carrick, who guided United to Champions League qualification as interim manager last season, struggling to prove he is the man for the job in the long term, who are the most likely candidates to replace the 45-year-old at Old Trafford if he fails to inspire a change of fortune?

Here are the managers who could be on United's radar -- and the prospects of them being the next one to take on one of the sport's biggest, and toughest, jobs.

Eddie Howe (unattached)

Positives

The 48-year-old is taking a break from the game after stepping down as Newcastle United manager in August following almost five years in charge. During his time at St James' Park, Howe saved the club from relegation before guiding the team to Champions League qualification on two occasions and ending a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy by winning the Carabao Cup in 2025.

Howe is a proven Premier League manager with a track record at Newcastle and Bournemouth. He is a team builder, tactically astute and his ability to transform the fortunes of players like Joelinton and Dan Burn at Newcastle would appeal to United, whose squad is stacked with players who are failing to live up to their potential. Another key element with Howe is his immediate availability.

Negatives

Howe will deliver stability and consistency wherever he manages, but does he possess the X factor for a club of United's magnitude? That is perhaps a harsh question to ask of a coach whose credentials are without question, but United need a coach to lift the whole club and its fan base. Howe's "Steady Eddie" persona might be exactly what they need, but also what they really don't need right now.

That strange dilemma is probably why United are in the mess they are in. They need the stability and calmness -- and direction -- that Howe would bring, but they also need a personality to become the focal point and leader of a club that has lost direction. Howe wins on the basics, but United need more than that.

Suitability rating

3/5: Howe would be a sensible appointment, but that isn't enough for Manchester United.

Antonio Conte (unattached)

articles.headline: PSG's Luis Enrique on stopping Barcelona: Keep ball away from Lamine Yamal
articles.description: Luis Enrique said Paris Saint-Germain will stop Lamine Yamal by not letting Barcelona have the ball when the two teams meet in a heavyweight UCL clash.
articles.body:
Luis Enrique said Paris Saint-Germain will stop Lamine Yamal by not letting Barcelona have the ball when the two teams meet in a heavyweight Champions League clash on Tuesday.

Recent meetings between the sides, including PSG's 2-1 win in Barcelona last year, have been characterised by Yamal's battle with left-back Nuno Mendes.

However, with Portugal international Mendes missing the fixture through injury, Yamal is likely to come up against Lucas Digne, although Luis Enrique says it will be up to the collective to counter the Barça winger's strengths.

"The best way to stop Lamine Yamal is to keep the ball away from Barcelona," Luis Enrique said in the pre-game news conference Monday.

"If he cannot get the ball, everything is calm. That would be ideal, but we know it won't be the case because it is difficult to play against Barcelona and Lamine Yamal.

"The way to defend a team with their quality is to be wary and approach it as a team. But it's not just Lamine. There's Raphinha, Pedri...there are a lot of top players."

Yamal, 19, has been in fine form this season, scoring nine goals and providing 10 assists as Barça have won all 11 of their matches in all competitions.

Since he burst on to the scene as a 15-year-old, he has been frequently compared to Lionel Messi, given he plays in the same position and now wears the No.10 shirt, but Luis Enrique, who coached Messi at Barça, warned against that analogy.

"I think Lamine wants to be Lamine and he is doing very well," he said. "He is improving in every aspect of his game, but if you compare him with the best player ever, there will only be one winner.

"Maybe we can speak in the future about that, but right now it is best not to compare him with Messi."

Tuesday's meeting at the Parc des Princes is a mouthwatering affair which pits back-to-back European champions PSG against the continent's in-form team Barcelona.

The LaLiga leaders have not only won every game they have played this season, but have done so scoring a remarkable 48 goals, averaging over four per match.

Both teams have also won their opening two Champions League fixtures, but despite the expectation the game is generating, Luis Enrique downplayed the significance of the result.

"The structure of the competition allows this game to be played now, but it doesn't show what the future may look like," the PSG coach said.

"I know we are both among the favourites, but there are other teams as well. This is just getting started.

"The competition will start in April, not now. And the teams that are there in April will compete for the trophy. This will be a very competitive match, but it's just three points at stake."

It is an especially emotional tie for Luis Enrique, who has an extensive history with Barça, but he says he will be able to leave that to one side on Tuesday.

articles.headline: PSG-Barcelona Champions League match to go ahead despite France protests
articles.description: The showpiece UCL match between PSG and Barcelona will go ahead as planned on Tuesday in Paris despite a weekend of violent protests.
articles.body:
PARIS -- The showpiece Champions League match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona will go ahead as planned on Tuesday in the French capital city, the French Interior minister confirmed, despite a weekend of protests marred by violence and looting across the country.

Many French citizens have been left shocked by the images of violence that have drawn worldwide attention and highlighted the country's tense social climate. On Monday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he has instructed prefects to impose "very limited" and "localized" curfews in cities to prevent more rioting and looting.

The violence targeted city halls, other public buildings and hundreds of businesses across the country, leading to more than 2,000 arrests.

Tuesday's match between PSG and Barcelona at the Parc des Princes will require a robust security deployment, with police forces already strained following weeks of student protests. In May, Paris police detained dozens of people after violence disrupted celebrations of PSG's second Champions League title win and a group tried to storm a police station in the French capital.

Speaking after an emergency meeting with top government officials, Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said the possibility of calling off planned events was discussed, including football matches.

"But this does not apply to tomorrow's match between PSG and FC Barcelona," he said, adding that other matches planned in European competitions this week would not be affected. Nuñez mentioned the match between Lille and Galatasaray scheduled Wednesday in the northern city, where looters also vandalized shops over the weekend.

Nuñez offered his resignation on Sunday but French President Emmanuel Macron asked him to stay to respond to police needs in an emergency situation. Macron instructed Nuñez "to take all necessary steps to ensure full transparency about the failures in planning and intelligence-gathering that led to the violence."

Lecornu said details of the areas to be placed under curfew will be provided later.

Nuñez acknowledged that authorities had "lost control" in some major cities on Saturday, with hundreds of businesses looted.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA free agency: Grades for offseason signings, extensions
articles.description: We're grading the most important offseason signings, including Cason Wallace's $139 million extension with the Thunder.
articles.body:
The NBA offseason still features plenty of important moves across the league.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Oct. 18: Thunder, Wallace agree to long-term extension

Cason Wallace terms: Five years, $139 million

Grade: B-

Wallace's contract, worth $27.8 million per year, is right in line with the going rate for young, defense-first perimeter players. Other recent rookie extensions include $31 million per year for Ausar Thompson, $30 million per year for Jalen Suggs and $25 million per year for Dyson Daniels.

Granted, the extensions for Suggs and Daniels haven't aged especially well since they were signed, given both players' offensive regressions.

There's good reason for the Thunder to believe Wallace is worth this contract, however, in a vacuum: A second-team All-Defensive honoree last season with one of the highest annual steal rates, he's one of the NBA's best perimeter stoppers, and he seems to have yet-untapped offensive potential, as well. He has never averaged more than 8.6 points in a season, but he's a career 37% 3-point shooter. And over a 15-game stretch last winter, mostly with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sidelined, Wallace averaged 13.9 points and 4.7 assists while assuming much greater offensive responsibilities.

The Thunder are betting there's more where that burst came from, now that Wallace is presumably set to take Luguentz Dort's spot in the starting lineup. He can defend most of the same stars Dort used to guard, while adding more offensive oomph and playmaking against elite defenses. In the conference finals against San Antonio, for example, Dort averaged 4.3 points and made 20% of his 3s, while Wallace averaged 10.1 points and made 50% of his 3s.

But this extension doesn't come in a vacuum; rather, it comes amid a threatening financial backdrop for Oklahoma City, which already had to trade Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe this summer for financial reasons. And the purse strings could get even tighter next year, when Gilgeous-Alexander's supermax extension kicks in.

To that end, one of the most important executive quotes of this summer came from the Thunder's Sam Presti, who told Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman, "The impression I have been given is that the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be reallocated to future teams."
